audit: The manager analogy clarifies ownership, yet the existing organizational diagrams can still leave readers equating a worker report with a completed refund. Lesson A puts different evidence fragments into three owned containers, including the exact missing link that prevents the supervisor from finishing the case. Lesson B turns the global budget rule into a reservation ledger with unused funds released only after settlement. Readers calculate whether another delegation fits rather than assuming each worker receives a fresh allowance. Both lessons preserve report provenance, limit worker authority and keep the supervisor accountable for the overall outcome without asserting that multiple agents automatically improve quality.

lessons.title: Three desks, one unresolved refund
lessons.intro: ShopAssist investigates order O-481. The payment worker found two captures; the policy worker found an exception. The supervisor must reconcile both before drafting an action.

relations: Workers return evidence; owner validates scope.
Missing shipment evidence blocks final synthesis.

read: Both captures match the order but do not explain their purpose.
The policy report names an exception requiring another fact.
The supervisor owns resolving that gap and any later action proposal.
lessons.question: Can two matching captures alone establish that USD 42 should be refunded?
lessons.answer: No. Two captures support a possible duplicate, but the separate-shipment exception remains unresolved. The supervisor needs authorized shipment evidence before deciding eligibility; an eventual refund still requires independent policy and execution checks.
lessons.takeaway: Merge qualifications with findings, not just conclusions.
lessons.assumption: Fictional records; workers have read-only capabilities. The containers describe ownership, not a required three-model architecture.

lessons.title: A child worker cannot mint a new budget
lessons.intro: One investigation starts with USD 1.00 available for delegated work. The supervisor reserves money before dispatch and releases only the unused portion after verified settlement.

data.rule: Available = total limit - settled spend - outstanding reservations; all children share it.

read: The first reservation leaves USD 0.70 available before the worker runs.
Settlement releases USD 0.12, not the entire USD 0.30.
Final spend is USD 0.53, leaving USD 0.47 for all remaining work.
lessons.question: May a new worker reserve USD 0.50 after these settlements?
lessons.answer: No. Only USD 0.47 remains, so the supervisor must reduce the bounded allocation or stop. A nested delegation consumes the same parent budget rather than resetting it.
lessons.takeaway: Account for every child against one owned budget.
lessons.assumption: Constructed costs; reservations are atomic and enforceable. Actual charges settle once. This ledger tracks money, not concurrent execution permits.
